judge_reasoning: Temmet and the second Knight token both entered the battlefield this turn and lack haste, so neither can attack. Only the original Knight can attack, dealing at most 4 damage after Temmet’s trigger, which is not lethal. Additionally, the stated mana payment for Anguished Unmaking omits its generic {1} cost, though sufficient mana was available.
model_solution:
1. Main phase: Tap one Irrigated Farmland for {W} and one for {U}; cast Temmet, Vizier of Naktamun.
2. Activate Gideon's 0 ability: create a second Knight Ally token (each Knight is 2/2, 3/3 with the emblem).
3. Tap an Irrigated Farmland for {W} and a Swamp for {B}; cast Anguished Unmaking targeting Seraph of the Suns (flying, indestructible blocker exiled; you lose 3 life, which is irrelevant).
4. Tap a Swamp for {B}; cast Dead Weight targeting Labyrinth Guardian. Its "when this creature becomes the target of a spell, sacrifice it" trigger resolves and it is sacrificed (Dead Weight then fizzles, which is fine).
5. Enter combat. Temmet's beginning-of-combat trigger targets a Knight token: it gets +1/+1 and can't be blocked this turn (now 4/4 unblockable).
6. Attack with Temmet (3/3) and both Knight tokens (4/4 unblockable and 3/3).
7. The only remaining potential blocker is Sparring Mummy (3/3), which can block only one attacker. The 4/4 Knight can't be blocked at all, and whichever of Temmet or the other 3/3 Knight goes unblocked deals 3. Opponent takes at least 4 + 3 = 7 damage, dropping from 7 to 0. You win.

Puzzle conventions:
Winning
Unless otherwise stated, you must win the puzzle by inflicting lethal damage to your opponent before the turn ends. This can be as late as during the cleanup step if necessary. Your solution must work for all possible outcomes, such as your opponent’s actions and blocking decisions (see below.)
Phase
Unless otherwise stated, you begin each puzzle at the beginning of your first main phase. You have already drawn a card and gone past upkeep triggers. You have not yet played a land, cast any spells, activated any abilities of permanents on the battlefield, or attacked.
Your Opponent’s Resources / Actions
Unless otherwise stated, your opponent has no cards in hand and no other permanents in play (including no lands – despite the lack of realism there.) This means the only actions you need to consider are activated abilities with no mana cost. Most puzzles with opponent actions will offer more information on this.
Blocking
You cannot assume that your opponent will block a certain way, unless they are somehow forced to. Your solution must satisfy all possible blocking scenarios, even ones that would seem strange in a regular game, and always deal lethal in order to be correct.
Dice
Sometimes you will see six-sided dice placed on cards. These are meant to indicate counters, of whatever type is most reasonable to be there. On most creatures they will be +1/+1 counters, on most artifacts and lands they will be charge counters, and on most Planeswalkers they will be loyalty counters.
If the card specifies a type of counter itself, however (like Icatian Javelineers or Raging Ravine), that will dictate which type it is. 
For -1/-1 counters, we will use a separate graphic to avoid confusion.
Zones
Unless otherwise stated, all zones not displayed are empty. Neither you nor your opponent have cards in graveyards or in exile.
Cards Drawn from Libraries
In any puzzle in which either player might draw cards or otherwise access their library, the puzzle will stipulate some known or assumed information about the library.
Most commonly, this will be a statement that you should assume that the cards remaining in libraries are to be assumed to be irrelevant to the puzzle.
Your Life
Occasionally, your own life total might appear to matter – for cards like Anguished Unmaking, for example. If we require you to consider your own life total in a puzzle, it will be displayed.
If your life total is not shown, you may assume it is irrelevant and effectively infinite.

When you are ready to answer, put your final winning line inside <solution> tags:

<solution>
1. First step...
2. Second step...
</solution>

Your line must be legal under the rules and must win against all possible opponent responses and blocking decisions.

content.thinking:
Let me analyze. Opponent at 7 life. Their creatures: Seraph of the Suns 4/4 flying indestructible, Sparring Mummy 3/3, Labyrinth Guardian 2/3 (dies if targeted by a spell).

My battlefield: Gideon AoZ (4 loyalty), emblem +1/+1, Knight Ally token 2/2 (so 3/3 with emblem), Behind the Scenes (skulk + {4}{W}: creatures get +1/+1 until EOT), 4 Irrigated Farmland, 3 Swamps. Hand: Illusory Wrappings, Dead Weight, Temmet, Anguished Unmaking.

Note: opponent has no lands, so their creatures... wait, they can't do anything. Opponent has no cards in hand, no other permanents. Activated abilities with no mana cost — Sparring Mummy, Labyrinth Guardian have none relevant. Seraph none.

Mana available: 4 Farmlands (W or U each), 3 Swamps = 7 mana.

Total mana: 7.

Plan: Make Gideon a creature? Gideon +1 makes him 5/5 indestructible. Attack with Gideon 5/5, plus Knight token.

Opponent at 7. Need lethal damage.

Key tools: Behind the Scenes gives skulk — creatures with power less than smallest defending creature's power can't be blocked. Seraph 4/4, Mummy 3/3, Guardian 2/3 (3/3? no 2/3, power 2). Skulk: blocked if power <= blocker's power... skulk means creature can't be blocked by creatures with greater power. So a creature with skulk and power 1 or less can't be blocked by any of their creatures (min power 2... actually Guardian power 2). Wait Guardian is 2/3, power 2. So skulk creature with power 1 can't be blocked by anyone (all blockers have power ≥ 2).

Temmet: at beginning of combat, target creature token you control gets +1/+1 and can't be blocked. Cast Temmet (2 mana WU), then at combat, give Knight token +1/+1 (making it 2/2 +1 emblem +1 Temmet = 4/4?) Wait Knight token 2/2, emblem +1/+1 → 3/3. Temmet trigger +1/+1 → 4/4, unblockable. Attack with Temmet (2/2 +1 = 3/3) and Knight 4/4.

Temmet 3/3 could be blocked by Guardian (2/3)? Temmet power 3, Guardian power 2 — Guardian can't block a creature with power greater... normal blocking has no power restriction; any creature can block. So Temmet 3/3 blocked by Guardian 2/3: Guardian dies (3 dmg), Temmet survives (2 dmg vs 3 toughness? Temmet is 2/2+1 emblem = 3/3, takes 2, survives). Or blocked by Mummy 3/3: trade. Or Seraph: Temmet dies, Seraph indestructible anyway.

Knight is unblockable, deals 4. Opponent at 7 → 3. Not enough alone.

Total damage possible: Gideon as 5/5 creature (via +1) — but +1 and 0 can't both be done... we can activate +1 once (one activation per turn). Gideon 5/5 +1/+1 emblem = 6/6 indestructible attacking. Plus Knight token 4/4 unblockable via Temmet = 4 damage. 6+4 = 10 ≥ 7. But Gideon can be blocked — that's fine, he's indestructible, but damage to opponent: if blocked, no damage to opponent.

Wait, but Gideon +1 makes him a creature but attacking with him... he's still a planeswalker; opponent's creatures can block. 6/6 blocked by Seraph 4/4 indestructible — no trample, so no damage to opponent. Blocked by Mummy 3/3: Mummy dies, no damage through. So Gideon could be fully blocked. Knight 4/4 unblockable deals 4, not lethal (7 life).

So need more unblockable/skulk damage, or remove blockers.

Options to deal with blockers:
- Dead Weight on Mummy: 3/3 → 1/1 (or dies? -2/-2 → 1/1, survives).
- Illusory Wrappings on Mummy: 0/2 base, +0 = 0/2. On Guardian: 0/3 base → 0/2? Illusory Wrappings sets base P/T to 0/2, so Guardian becomes 0/2 (+0). Note Guardian dies when targeted by a spell! So casting Illusory Wrappings or Dead Weight on Labyrinth Guardian kills it (sacrifice trigger).
- Anguished Unmaking: exile nonland permanent — but our life isn't shown, so we can pay 3 life. Exile Seraph of the Suns!

Seraph is the main blocker (flying, indestructible). Our attackers: all could be blocked by any of the three creatures though (ground).

Plan A:
1. Cast Temmet (W U) — 2 mana. Land total 7 mana, used 2, 5 left.
2. Activate Gideon 0: create Knight token (2/2, 3/3 with emblem). Now 5 mana still... 0 loyalty ability costs nothing. Wait we have 7 mana total, Temmet used 2, leaving 5.
3. Anguished Unmaking (1WB) exile Seraph — 3 mana, leaving 2.
4. Dead Weight (B) on Labyrinth Guardian — it dies (sacrifice trigger). Leaving 1 mana.
5. Combat: Temmet trigger target Knight token (one of them) — +1/+1, unblockable. That Knight is 2/2+1(emb)+1 = 4/4.

Attackers: Gideon? No, we used 0 ability; Gideon stays planeswalker. Attack with Temmet (3/3), Knight A (4/4 unblockable), Knight B (3/3).

Blockers: Sparring Mummy 3/3 only (Seraph exiled, Guardian dead).

Opponent must block: Knight B (3/3) blocked by Mummy: trade, no damage. Knight A unblockable: 4 damage. Temmet 3/3 blocked by Mummy too? Mummy can only block one attacker. Opponent at 7, takes 4 from Knight A. If they don't block Knight B, they take 4+3 = 7... Temmet 3/3 gets through if Mummy blocks Knight B: 4 + 3 = 7. Lethal!

Wait: attackers total: Temmet 3/3, KnightA 4/4 (unblockable), KnightB 3/3. Mummy can block one. Opponent takes at least 4 (KnightA) + 3 (from either Temmet or KnightB, whichever unblocked) = 7. Lethal!

But wait — mana check: Temmet {W}{U} = 2, Anguished Unmaking {1}{W}{B} = 3, Dead Weight {B} = 1. Total 6 ≤ 7. Good.

But Anguished Unmaking costs 3 life — our life is not shown, assume irrelevant/infinite. But hold on: opponent could have... no responses.

Also check: can opponent double-block? Mummy 3/3 can only block one creature. Could Guardian have been kept alive and used? We killed it with Dead Weight — actually Dead Weight targeting Guardian causes sacrifice ("When this creature becomes the target of a spell, sacrifice it"). Yes, targeting triggers it, it's sacrificed. Good. Note: Dead Weight would go on stack, Guardian's trigger resolves, sacrificed before Dead Weight resolves — Dead Weight fizzles since target illegal? That's fine, we wasted 1 mana but Guardian dies.

Actually alternative: use Illusory Wrappings on Mummy (0/2), and Dead Weight... let's stick with plan A.

Wait — one issue: does Temmet's trigger require target creature token — yes, Knight token. Timing: "At the beginning of combat on your turn" — triggers when we declare combat phase. Fine.

Also alternative check: could opponent block KnightA despite unblockable? No.

Damage calc with emblem: Knight token 2/2 → 3/3. +Temmet trigger → 4/4. Yes.

Temmet 2/2 + emblem = 3/3. Knight B 3/3.

Mummy blocks one of Temmet/KnightB. The other deals 3. 4+3 = 7 = lethal. 

But wait, does opponent's life = 7, damage 7 → 0. Yes.

Hmm, but what if Mummy blocks Temmet or Knight B and... they have only one creature. Could they block with Mummy and also have Seraph? Exiled. Guardian dead. Only Mummy.

Actually wait — do we even need to kill Guardian? Attackers: Temmet 3/3, KnightA 4/4 unblockable, KnightB 3/3. If we don't remove Guardian and Seraph: Seraph blocks KnightB (3/3 dies to 4/4... wait KnightB 3/3 blocked by Seraph 4/4: KnightB dies, Seraph indestructible). Guardian 2/3 blocks Temmet 3/3: Guardian dies. Mummy 3/3 blocks KnightA? Can't — unblockable. So KnightA deals 4. Total 4 < 7. Need removal.

Alternative Plan B: Instead of Temmet, use Behind the Scenes' {4}{W}: creatures get +1/+1. And skulk. Hmm, Plan A works.

Double-check Anguished Unmaking legality: exile Seraph (nonland permanent). Lose 3 life — fine.

Actually, let me reconsider order: cast Temmet before combat so it's on battlefield to trigger. Yes, cast in main phase.

Mana sources: 4 Irrigated Farmland (W or U), 3 Swamps (B). Temmet needs W,U; Unmaking needs 1,W,B; Dead Weight B. Total: 2 W, 1 U, 1 B generic... Let's count colored: W:2 (Temmet, Unmaking), U:1, B:2 (Unmaking, Dead Weight). Total 6 mana: tap Farmland(W) for W, Farmland(U) for U, Farmland(W) for W, Swamp B, Swamp B... Unmaking needs 1 generic: use third... Farmlands: 4 available. Tap: FW, FU, FW, SW, SB = 6 mana. Fine.

One more consideration: could opponent sac Guardian themselves or anything? No abilities.

Also, Gideon's 0 ability creating second Knight: we start with one Knight token already on battlefield. Yes, "Knight Ally token" is on battlefield. So we don't even need Gideon's 0! Wait — we need two knights? Actually we need total damage: KnightA unblockable 4 + one more attacker for 3. We have Temmet himself (3/3). So attackers: Temmet 3/3, Knight 4/4 unblockable. Blockers after removal: Mummy only. Mummy blocks Temmet → Temmet dies (3/3 vs 3/3 trade), Knight deals 4. 4 < 7. Not enough!

So we DO need the second Knight token from Gideon's 0. Correct: Gideon 0 creates second Knight. Then attackers: Temmet, KnightA (unblockable 4/4), KnightB (3/3). Mummy blocks one of the 3-power creatures, other gets through for 3. Total 7. 

Verify Temmet trigger targets a token — target KnightA. Yes.

Edge: What if opponent blocks KnightB with Mummy and Temmet... only one Mummy. Right.

Could opponent take damage assignment tricks? No, just chump block.

So solution:
1. Main phase: tap lands, cast Temmet (WU).
2. Gideon 0: create Knight token (now 3/3 with emblem).
3. Cast Anguished Unmaking targeting Seraph of the Suns (lose 3 life).
4. Cast Dead Weight targeting Labyrinth Guardian — its trigger sacrifices it.
5. Declare combat. Temmet trigger: target Knight token gets +1/+1 and can't be blocked (4/4 unblockable).
6. Attack with Temmet, both Knights. Mummy can block only one; unblockable Knight deals 4, and at least one of Temmet/KnightB (3/3 each) is unblocked for 3. Total ≥7 → opponent at 0.

Wait, verify Dead Weight targeting: "When this creature becomes the target of a spell, sacrifice it." Dead Weight on stack, Guardian becomes target, trigger triggers, resolves, sacrifice. Guardian gone. Dead Weight countered on resolution (target illegal). Fine.

Alternatively, save a mana: no need.

Also confirm: can opponent's Mummy block Temmet (legendary 3/3)? Yes, but trades. Either way 3 damage gets through.

Damage total: min scenario: Mummy blocks Temmet (both die) or KnightB (trade). Unblocked attacker deals 3. KnightA deals 4. Total 7. Opponent at 7 → 0. Win.

Also double-check skulk/Behind the Scenes not needed. Correct.

One check on Gideon 0 ability: creates token at sorcery speed — we're in main phase, fine. Gideon at 4 loyalty, 0 ability: loyalty stays 4. Fine.

Embalm irrelevant.
